title: what is the best AI to help you code in Unity3D?
author: ziadd_hh
selftext:
i want to build a game and publish it to the playstore and appstore. it would be pursuit chasing car game. you buy cars then go in an endless road while police chase you and try to slam and lower your health you until you crash. thats the core idea of the game.

it would have IAP and Rewarded ads too. but the only problem is that i dont know how to code. i have the UI and models ready. i just curious about using AI for the coding part and for guiding me what to do because learning C# would take alot of time and i want to publish the game fast (i already know basics of C# tho).

saw a lot of people say Claude is best for coding. or is there any better? what's your best advice should i learn more? or just use Ai for coding and guiding in what to do?

and about the IAP and Ads. can AI handle that safely? of should i do them by self.

comments.author: meischix
comments.body: You can use Claude Opus 4.6 on any AI-powered IDE that lets you pick any of the big models. For plan mode, you can go for Sonnet or Gemini. But when executing, use Opus. And don't forget to use a good MCP for Unity. Of the MCPs I've tried, I found this MCP on the link more useful because it has a very active Discord community and a very active author behind it (https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP).

replies.author: SlimPerceptions
replies.body: How capable is this MCP, in your experience?

replies.author: meischix
replies.body:
I had a lot of success using it in tandem with Anthropic models. I'm using Cursor, btw. I almost one-shotted my Global Game Jam game with it. It could have been better if I meta-prompted my one shot.

Back in January, it was a bit quick in spending my tokens, but that changed after they added the MCP skills. Connecting it is a breeze as well, plus if anything went wrong, the author almost always immediately helps out on Discord.

replies.author: SlimPerceptions
replies.body: Wow I had no idea it would be that good at spatial reasoning. I’ll need to try it out

replies.author: Content_Ad6829
replies.body: is it better than this one here [unity-mcp](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp)?

replies.author: meischix
replies.body: I haven't tried that one yet. Though at the end of the day, they're all tools. My advice is usually to pick one that works best for you and run with it.

replies.author: Ok-Version-8996
replies.body: Can you explain MCP to a guy who is just using opus to make prompts for Claude code and knows nothing else?

replies.author: meischix
replies.body:
So Cursor, Claude Code, and similar AI-powered IDEs or agentic vibe-coding tools usually have a general knowledge of coding, but not the specific instructions to use a certain tool, for example. So if you code on them straight, you'll usually get mixed results and might even wrestle with it. To fix that, you need a Model Context Protocol. In this case, it "teaches" the tool the proper coding standards and other critical info to properly use Unity.

TL;DR Cursor, Claude code etc., are like talented junior developers with zero knowledge of how to use Unity. The MCP teaches it how to use Unity.

replies.body:

comments.author: propnalysis
comments.body:
claude is genuinely the best for unity coding right now, paste your script, describe what you want it to do, and it'll usually get you 80-90% of the way there even on complex stuff like IAP and rewarded ads integration. cursor is also worth using as an IDE because it has claude built in and can see your whole project context which makes the back and forth way faster. the IAP and ads side is actually one of the easier things to get AI help with because unity gaming services and admob have well documented APIs that claude has seen a lot of, just be thorough about describing which SDK you're using.  
  
the honest advice though is that using AI for 100% of your code without understanding any of it will slow you down eventually, not because AI is bad but because when something breaks you won't know where to look. learning just enough to read what it generates makes the whole process smoother. if you want to move even faster than unity allows, codewisp ai lets you build and publish web games just by describing what you want which might be worth trying to get a feel for the core loop before committing to the full mobile build.

replies.author: ziadd_hh
replies.body: i really appreciate your advice and i would be testing first just to understand everything on how to use AI in game dev and will try to learn more C#

comments.author: Extra_Blacksmith674
comments.body:
I'm using codex and it just works. I give the project directory to it as a workspace and it is now writing 90% of the code, sometimes I have to step in or throw away a few hours work, but it works really well. 

I added some editor code that lets me copy gameobject id's in the scene so I can just paste those into codex and tell it to do whatever work that needs to be done on it. Within reason :) anything artistic forget about it.

comments.author: propnalysis
comments.body:
ghost of tsushima and dishonored 2 are must plays if u haven't already, that same "stealth is optional but so satisfying" energy. hitman trilogy also goes crazy hard for this, and if u liked splinter cell specifically then chaos theory still holds up better than most modern games tbh  
  
lowkey all these games got me so into game design mechanics that i started experimenting w building my own stuff. codewisp lets u go from idea to actual playable web game just by describing what u want, no coding needed. pretty wild how fast u can prototype a stealth concept w it
